description: Builds the Jaccard tag-distance matrix that cluster_tags feeds into agglomerative clustering, per FORMULATION.md section 6's locked clustering method (Jaccard tag-distance, no genre anchor). Factored out as its own testable unit since the matrix construction (which entities are the clustered 'points', and how per-game tag sets become per-tag co-occurrence vectors) is a distinct, independently verifiable step from the clustering call itself.
docstring:
Build a tag-by-tag Jaccard distance matrix from tag co-occurrence.

Args:
    tags: game_tags-shaped rows (appid, tag, votes, rank) for the run's candidate set, already filtered to tags with votes >= AnalysisParams.min_tag_votes by the caller (cluster_tags).

Returns:
    A square, symmetric DataFrame indexed and columned by the distinct tag strings present in `tags`, where cell (t1, t2) = 1 - |games(t1) ∩ games(t2)| / |games(t1) ∪ games(t2)| (Jaccard DISTANCE, i.e. 1 minus Jaccard similarity, so 0 = identical game sets, 1 = no games in common). Diagonal is exactly 0.0 for every tag against itself.

Note:
    'Games' here means each tag's SET OF APPIDS that carry it (after the min_tag_votes and max_tags_per_game filtering already applied upstream in extract_tags/the caller) -- clustering groups TAGS into archetypes based on how similarly they co-occur across games, and cluster_tags subsequently assigns each GAME to an archetype via its own tags' cluster memberships (majority/plurality vote among a game's tags' clusters -- see cluster_tags for that assignment rule). This two-step tag-then-game structure is this spec's own interpretation of 'archetype is a tag cluster... not a single tag' (FORMULATION.md section 6); the module_spec.json does not spell out this tag-vs-game clustering distinction explicitly.
preconditions: tags has no duplicate (appid, tag) pairs
Every distinct tag in tags is associated with at least one appid (trivially true by construction)
postconditions: The returned matrix is symmetric: D[t1,t2] == D[t2,t1]

edge_cases.input: Two tags that always co-occur on exactly the same set of games
Two tags that never co-occur on any game
A tag used by exactly one game
edge_cases.expected_behavior: still produces valid, finite distances against every other tag (Jaccard is well-defined as long as the union is non-empty, which it always is for two tags each used by at least one game)
returns an empty (0x0) DataFrame, not an error

unit_tests.name: test_identical_game_sets_zero_distance
unit_tests.description: Two tags applied to exactly the same 3 games have distance 0.0.

unit_tests.name: test_disjoint_game_sets_max_distance
unit_tests.description: Two tags applied to completely disjoint game sets have distance 1.0.

unit_tests.name: test_matrix_is_symmetric
unit_tests.description: For a synthetic multi-tag fixture, D equals its own transpose.

unit_tests.name: test_empty_tags_returns_empty_matrix
unit_tests.description: An empty tags frame returns a 0x0 DataFrame.
